speakingSourceEnglish: Tell a barista you are going to eat here, ask if you can sit on the terrace, and ask if you can pay by card.
speakingObjectives: Tell a barista that you are going to eat here, using Je vais manger sur place or an equivalent.
Ask if you can sit on the terrace, using Est-ce que je peux m'asseoir en terrasse ?
Ask if you can pay by card, using Est-ce que je peux payer par carte ?
sourceNotes: frenchCards holds one French face for each of the 15 source cards, in source order (cards 1-9 kind 'term', cards 10-15 kind 'phrase'). Source English and kinds are not restated or edited; they map by 1-based index.
frenchReader holds one French reading for each of the 9 Reader lines, in source order, with the Emma and Diego speaker labels kept. Reader English maps by 1-based index and is not edited.
readerTitleFrench renders the source passage title 'Desayuno en Oaxaca'. The source gives no English title. The title is the only place the Oaxaca setting is stated.

Card 15 was changed from 'Faites-vous les œufs à la commande ?' to 'Est-ce que vous faites des œufs au choix ?'. It follows the Spanish 'al gusto' and the source note ('eggs cooked the way you like'), keeps faire for the hacer focus, and matches the est-ce que pattern of cards 13-14. The Haiku notes defending 'à la commande' and rejecting 'à la demande' were removed as unsound.
Reader line 2 was changed from 'fait le café' to 'fait du café', because the Spanish 'hace café' and the English 'makes coffee' have no article. Faire is kept for the hacer focus.
Reader line 4 was changed to 'C'est pour manger sur place, pas à emporter.' to carry 'comer' from the Spanish 'para comer aquí'. Card 9 stays 'sur place', the standard counter term.
Reader line 9 keeps 'pour acheter du pain'. This adds a verb that 'por pan' and 'for bread' do not have; the Haiku note calling it more precise was removed.
Diego's 'vous pouvez' matches the Spanish usted form 'puede'. Emma's 'je peux' matches 'puedo'.
'le café' is both the place (card 2, Reader line 1) and the drink (Reader line 2).

forms holds six Reader-line pairs in Reader order (lines 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 9), covering aller + infinitive, faire and pouvoir. The english and readerLine fields both hold the exact source Reader English, speaker labels included.

Card-only patterns are not in forms because forms is limited to Reader lines: plain aller à (card 10), nous allons + infinitive (card 12) and vous faites (card 15). Pedir is in the source verb list but outside the stated focus.

modes holds six entries with the unique labels see, recall, hear, type, say and write. Each targetEnglish is the exact source English at that sourceType and sourceIndex. Card 15 is kept out of modes while its source disagreement is open.

Speaking objective 1 has no verbatim card. 'Je vais manger sur place' is built from card 9, aller + infinitive and Reader line 4. Haiku's fourth speaking objective was removed because it is not in the source speaking task.
qualifiedReviewResiduals: Source disagreement on card 15: the English 'eggs to order' means cooked when ordered, while the Spanish 'al gusto' means cooked the way you like. They are not exact equivalents. The French follows the Spanish sense, and the source English is left unedited.
'Est-ce que vous faites des œufs au choix ?' needs native review for naturalness as a spoken café question.
This is a private, unreviewed draft. No native French review has been done and no approval is claimed.
No audio is attached to this candidate. The hear and say modes have no audio asset in this candidate.
'C'est pour manger sur place' (Reader line 4) and 'Oui, vous pouvez' (Reader line 6) mirror the source closely and need a native check for naturalness in service speech.
'à emporter' and 'sur place' follow France usage; Québec equivalents are not included.
'chilaquiles' stays as a loan word in French.
'?' and ':' are preceded by a plain space. Whether to use non-breaking spaces (U+202F or U+00A0) is undecided, and it affects exact-match checking in type and write modes.
The source English 'the register' (card 6) is left unedited; the French 'la caisse' follows the Spanish 'la caja'.
All French is an unreviewed AI candidate; qualified French/domain review is required. The model triad is not approval.
